I think there are good reasons for citing a metrics page/site. Developers often want to be able to provide some evidence of the quality or popularity of a package and whilst being on CRAN does indicate a minimum standard, with the continuous CRAN checks being particularly valuable, other metrics can be useful. I presume this is why <@U055CT9LSR5> wants to cite the R Observatory, rather than just CRAN.

There are a couple of ways to do this - style guides provide standards for citing a website where the contents are designed to change over time, e.g. <https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines/references/examples/webpage-website-references#6|APA> would be something like:

HJJB, LLC. (n.d.), _R Observatory._ Retrieved August 5, 2026, from <https://r-observatory.thecoatlessprofessor.com/>.

for the whole site or

HJJB, LLC. (n.d.), _ggmice 0.1.1 ._ Retrieved August 5, 2026, from  <https://r-observatory.thecoatlessprofessor.com/>.

for the package page. If you added author information to the site, you could have Balamuta, J for the author, or specify some organization, e.g. R Observatory Organization. The bit in italics is the title, for which people would usually use whatever is in <h1> or what visually appears as the header - this is where you might give some guidance for a standard citation, maybe 'Metrics for ggmice version 0.1.1'.

The other approach is to treat the dashboard as software and provide a citation for the software itself or a related paper. Then someone might say 'These package metrics were obtained from the R Observatory (citation) on August 5, 2026'. Getting a Zenodo DOI is a good solution here as you can set this up quickly and you can keep a stable concept DOI regardless if the repository moves/maintainers change/the URL of the deployed instance changes. As long as you have a link to the dashboard on the repo pointed to by Zenodo you're all good.

Then longer term you might consider an R Journal paper - more appropriate than JSS here - accepting the whole process might take 1-2 years but you'll hopefully get some good feedback through the review process.

Whatever you decide, it would be good to have information on how to cite the dashboard on the dashboard itself. Package pages might have buttons to 'cite this package' giving result of citation() and 'cite this page' giving your preferred way to cite the site/page.

Thank you, this is very helpful!! I indeed want to cite the R Observatory because of the metrics it collates.

I very much agree that citing the package itself should not be via citing the dashboard. A 'cite this package' button would be great!

But rather because it is a single source to cite several metric (e.g., CRAN & conda downloads, as well as test coverage, etc.), which would be very convenient as a developer trying to show the impact of your work :slightly_smiling_face:
